Exercise A

Arrange the meeting

Breakout rooms, 25 minutes, groups of three. Your Fix Our Campus proposal has been shortlisted. Read the manager’s email, then choose your role. Each role has a private calendar: do not show it. Ask each other about your plans to find the best time. No time is perfect, so someone has to change an arrangement.

The email

From: Facilities Manager, Campus Services
Subject: Your Fix Our Campus proposal – meeting next week

Dear team,

Thank you for your proposal. The panel has shortlisted it, and I would like to meet your team for 45 minutes next week to discuss the next steps. I am available at these times:

Monday 30 Nov, 10:00 · Tuesday 1 Dec, 16:00 · Wednesday 2 Dec, 14:00 · Thursday 3 Dec, 11:00 · Friday 4 Dec, 09:00

All meetings are in Room B2.14. Please come as a whole team, in person if at all possible. I can only approve a budget if someone can answer my questions about costs.

Please reply by Thursday to confirm the time, who is coming, a short agenda (three points) and anything you would like me to prepare.

Best regards,
Facilities Manager

Key terms for today

agenda – the list of points to discuss in a meeting
availability – the times when someone is free
reschedule – to change the date or time of a meeting or appointment
postpone – to move an event to a later date
follow-up – an action or message after a meeting that continues what was agreed

Ask, don’t show

Are you doing anything on Monday morning? · What time does your shift finish? · Could you move it? · That doesn’t suit me, I’m afraid. · How about Tuesday instead? · Shall we say four o’clock, then?

Your group’s decision

Exercise B

Language for arranging

Exercise C

Confirm by email

On your own, 15 minutes. Write the reply to the Facilities Manager for your group. Use your group’s decision from Exercise A.

Word count: 0

Confirm the time and place, say who is coming, give your three-point agenda and ask for one thing to be prepared. Use at least four of these terms: agenda, availability, reschedule, postpone, follow-up.
